prompts: This is an exercise. Do not give away solutions; use https://inria.github.io/scikit-learn-mooc/python_scripts/02_numerical_pipeline_sol_00.html only to craft hints and guiding questions. This exercise practices the core scikit-learn fit/predict/score API by training a KNeighborsClassifier on the adult census numeric dataset and evaluating it on a separate held-out test set. Key learning objectives are: (1) looking up default hyperparameter values via documentation or the ? operator (default n_neighbors is 5); (2) instantiating a KNeighborsClassifier with n_neighbors=50 and calling fit on data and target from adult-census-numeric.csv; (3) using predict on the first 10 rows and comparing with actual targets; (4) computing training accuracy with score; (5) loading adult-census-numeric-test.csv into separate data_test and target_test variables and computing test accuracy by calling score on the already-fitted model. Expected outputs include: a trained model, a prediction array for the first 10 samples, a training accuracy (around 0.82), and a test accuracy (around 0.82). A critical pitfall to watch for: the test set must never be passed to fit; students should call score(data_test, target_test) on the model already trained on the training data. Calling fit again on the test data retrains the model entirely, producing a misleadingly different score that does not measure generalization. If asked about more information on the dataset, refer to https://inria.github.io/scikit-learn-mooc/python_scripts/datasets_adult_census.html
